0|264e56d8247ef6e31ed4386926cae86c61ddcb18|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"mm: disable user interface to manually rescue unevictable pages
At one point
column2: anonymous pages were supposed to go on the unevictable list

column1: when no swap space was configured
column2: and the idea was to manually rescue

column1: those pages after adding swap and making them evictable again.  But
nowadays
column2: swap-backed pages on the anon LRU list are not scanned without

column1: available swap space anyway
column2: so there is no point in moving them to a

column1: separate list anymore.
The manual rescue could also be used in case pages were stranded on the
unevictable list due to race conditions.  But the code has been around for
a while now and newly discovered bugs should be properly reported and
dealt with instead of relying on such a manual fixup.
In addition to the lack of a usecase
column2: the sysfs interface to rescue pages

column1: from a specific NUMA node has been broken since its introduction
unlikely that anybody ever relied on that.
This patch removes the functionality behind the sysctl and the
node-interface and emits a one-time warning when somebody tries to access
either of them.
